**In one line**: A research firm reportedly found that DeepSeek's new AI model is by far the cheapest to run among well-known models.

### Key points
- Per Reuters, a research firm's analysis concluded that the inference (run) cost of DeepSeek's new model is far lower than that of well-known rivals.
- Lower run costs mean the same workload can be served with less compute and expense, a gap that widens at deployment scale.
- DeepSeek, a China-based AI developer, has previously drawn attention for its low-cost training and operating approach.

### Why it matters
Run cost is a primary driver of the real bill for operating a model in production. If a best-in-class inference price holds up, unit economics — not just benchmark performance — could weigh more heavily in enterprises' model-adoption decisions.
